THE IDEA

Assign, average, repeat.

K-means groups unlabeled points into k clusters. K-means++ chooses initial centers from your data, favoring points far from centers already chosen. The seed makes this repeatable.

  1. Assign: compare each point with all centers and choose the nearest by Euclidean distance.
  2. Update: replace each center with the arithmetic mean of every point currently assigned to it.
  3. Repeat until assignments stop changing.

Use the step button to separate assignment from center movement. Colored point-to-center lines show membership. Click a cluster to highlight its members and see their mean. Inspect a point to compare its distances to all centers.

After a center update, point colors still show the previous assignment until the next assignment step. Background regions always show the nearest current center. Inertia is the sum of squared distances using the displayed assignments and centers.

All points participate; there is no training/test split or target color. Cluster colors are arbitrary IDs. Empty clusters keep their old centers, so fewer than k clusters may have members, especially with repeated coordinates. Exact distance ties retain the previous assignment if possible, otherwise they choose the first center.

K-means can settle on different solutions depending on initialization. It prefers compact groups and cannot recover concentric rings as separate clusters. Changing k, data, or seed resets clustering. Page navigation and reload start a new experiment.

Import points

Paste x,y columns with an optional header. Coordinates must be 0–1. Up to 1,000 rows; at least k points are needed to initialize. No color labels are required.
